25 A musical instrument called a bugle is a long tube with a mouthpiece at one end. The other end is
open and flared, as shown.
A musician maintains stationary sound waves with a node at the mouthpiece and an antinode at
the other end. The lowest frequency of sound that the bugle can produce is 92 Hz.
Which different frequencies of sound can be produced by the bugle?
A
92 Hz, 138 Hz, 184 Hz, 230 Hz, 276 Hz
B
92 Hz, 184 Hz, 276 Hz, 368 Hz, 460 Hz
C
92 Hz, 276 Hz, 460 Hz, 644 Hz, 828 Hz
D
92 Hz, 276 Hz, 828 Hz, 2484 Hz, 7452 Hz

hints: Notice the stated end conditions: a displacement node at the mouthpiece and an antinode at the flared open end, so the bugle acts as a pipe closed at one end.

Recall that a closed-open length $L$ can only hold an odd number of quarter wavelengths: $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4...$ so allowed frequencies are odd multiples of the $92 \text{ Hz}$ fundamental.
Test the lists by checking the second frequency: $2 \times 92 = 184 \text{ Hz}$ would need an even harmonic, while $3 \times 92 = 276 \text{ Hz}$ fits the odd-harmonic rule.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe: node at the mouthpiece means that end is effectively closed, antinode at the flared end means that end is open, with length $L$ fixed.
For a closed-open pipe the stationary wave must fit $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$ for $n = 1, 2, 3...$, giving $\lambda = 4L, 4L/3, 4L/5...$.
Since $f = v/\lambda$ with constant speed $v$, the frequencies are $f_n = (2n-1)v/4L = (2n-1)f_0$ where $f_0 = 92 \text{ Hz}$ is the lowest frequency.
Substitute odd numbers $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$: $1 \times 92 = 92 \text{ Hz}$, $3 \times 92 = 276 \text{ Hz}$, $5 \times 92 = 460 \text{ Hz}$, $7 \times 92 = 644 \text{ Hz}$, $9 \times 92 = 828 \text{ Hz}$.
Only the list $92 \text{ Hz}$, $276 \text{ Hz}$, $460 \text{ Hz}$, $644 \text{ Hz}$, $828 \text{ Hz}$ matches these odd harmonics. This is option C.

A.explanation: Gives steps of $46 \text{ Hz}$, including $138 \text{ Hz}$ and $184 \text{ Hz}$, which are not odd multiples of $92 \text{ Hz}$ and cannot satisfy node-antinode ends.

B.explanation: Gives all integer multiples $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ times $92 \text{ Hz}$, which is the pattern for a pipe open at both ends, not node at one end and antinode at the other.

C.explanation: Gives $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$ times $92 \text{ Hz}$, which are the odd harmonics required for a tube closed at one end and open at the other.

D.explanation: Multiplies by $3$ each time to give $92 \text{ Hz}$, $276 \text{ Hz}$, $828 \text{ Hz}$, but higher modes add $2f_0$, they do not multiply the previous frequency by $3$.
